rationale:
bugs_open/283 round 6 — the JUDGED pipeline (RFC_034's LLM quarter, owner-ruled) is BUILT, and building it exposed a defect in the APPROVED mechanical batch that this round also fixes: bugs_open/324. The converter's completeness check grepped for the literal forms its own passes rename, so a binding that carries an id to a lookup through a VARIABLE (var ids=['amount',…] → getElementById(id)), a config object ({id:'gsfc-accel'} → field.id), a helper (el('rw-ev')) or a CONCATENATION ('block-'+name) survived unrenamed on 32 of 69 converted rows — 14 serving live, structurally dead at load or first interaction, while every batch check (ids, tokens, duplicates, served-page spot-checks) read genuinely green. Measured with the Go detector over all 69 live rows and verified at robot-hands.com's served bytes. 27 repair mechanically; 5 route to the judged pool.

The change set (one commit): (1) pass 5 + an INDEPENDENT binding detector (UnprefixedBindings, incl. a composition-hazard check) wired INTO GateConvertedTemplate — the class cannot ship again; refuse-contexts (comparisons, case labels, object keys, computed access) are skipped and reported, never guessed. (2) fix_type repair_instance_scope_bindings — pass 5 for already-converted rows, gated by detector-empty + two-instance gate + comparative write guard, own change_source. (3) fix_type scope_component_instance_judged — the judged write: re-derives its baseline from the row, refuses on two-instance gate not fully clean / markup changed outside script bodies (derived expectation) / id-set drift / unprefixed bindings / collapse guard; refusals write NOTHING and land needs_human_review. (4) workflow migration 486_HOLD: fixer self-routes needs_script_scoping to a script-only LLM brief (sonnet 32k, tolerate_truncation deliberately absent) and chains create_rerender into an owned-page section_edit delivery (apply_section_edit binds InstanceID — closes 283 §13.6's gap for every template fix). (5) seed 487_HOLD: repair batch over all converted rows, derived at apply time, serving-broken rows priority 30. Both SQL files are _HOLD: they dispatch fix_types that exist only post-roll.

Why the judged writer is fan-out-intended and NOT tool-improver's fenced path: 22 of the 25 judged rows are component_level='section' and one (mortgages-repayment) is placed on two pages — sharedComponentWriteCheck refuses exactly that shape, correctly, for page-scoped findings; this is a component-subject fix. Declared in component_template_writer_coverage_test.go with the measurement cited.

Verification: full actions suite green on a git-archive-HEAD overlay (the working tree carries another session's WIP); fixtures are pinned LIVE bytes for all three defect classes plus one pre-conversion snapshot; mutation controls in both directions at the transform, the detector, and the wiring (pass 5 disabled → test fails; detector silenced → test fails). A false claim found in my own round-5-adjacent PLAN is corrected visibly and logged in WRONG_CALLS (the '25 fired during the batch' line).

plan.risks: (1) Markup-parity check may false-refuse on cosmetic LLM reformatting — chosen failure direction is refuse-to-human, never write; relax only on evidence (stated in the design). (2) apply_section_edit with empty field_updates re-rendering+deploying an LMC owned page is [UNVERIFIED] end-to-end on that estate — the canary is designed to prove it before the batch (PLAN §5). (3) The 4 serving automation-savings placements stay live-broken until the judged pipeline runs — if it slips, the contained alternative is a snapshot rollback of 3 rows + rerender (owner call, named in bugs_open/324). (4) Migration/seed are _HOLD: applying before the roll dispatches unknown fix_types; the files' headers carry the digest-verify precondition.
